comments.body:
I found no definite defect, but I can't establish safety. This is a large new multi-process NCCL/gloo tensor-parallel path that I can't run, and the GPU tests are skipped without two GPUs. Two risks need a human:

1. Failure handling can hang. `shutdown()` does a blocking `broadcast_object(("stop",))` with a 30-day timeout. `engine_core`'s new `finally` calls it even when the driver died mid-step. A worker may then be waiting in an all_reduce or broadcast_tensor instead of the object broadcast, so the collectives mismatch and the core process could deadlock while holding GPUs.
2. The `_forward` signature changed to accept `SchedulerOutput | bool`. The rest of its body, including the graph and piecewise runner paths, isn't visible, so I can't confirm nothing else reads `so` attributes when a worker passes a bool.

Also, `head_dim` became a dataclass field. Any `dataclasses.replace` elsewhere that changes `hidden_size` or `num_attention_heads` would now keep a stale `head_dim`.

comments.body:
Timestamp correctness depends on the Spark session time zone, and lakehouse/spark.py is not in the diff, so I cannot confirm it is UTC. The ISO parse (iso_ts) uses to_timestamp on a 'Z' string with no zone in the format, so it is read in the session zone. pipe_ts then applies to_utc_timestamp on top of a session-zone parse. If spark.sql.session.timeZone is not UTC, ts_utc is skewed and the gold boot-phase deltas that mix formats are wrong. Please confirm get_spark pins the zone to UTC.

I also could not check bronze.load_table or the bronze column names against what silver reads. config.table_path now raises KeyError for names outside the three table lists, which could break existing bronze callers I cannot see. A human should confirm these before deploy.

comments.body: applyLayout dispatches the renderer's 'apply-layout' control action, and the comments reference workspaceStore.applyLayoutPreset. Neither an 'apply-layout' handler in controlBridge.ts nor applyLayoutPreset in workspaceStore.ts appears in the visible diff, and the controlBridge hunk looks truncated after 'open-app'. If the handler does not already exist, the new arrange_windows tool will fail at runtime. A human should confirm that the handler exists and accepts all five presets.

openTerminal now uses the return value of openWindow() as a windowId. The diff does not show that openWindow returns a string id. Please verify its signature, since the 'terminal' path in open-app depends on it. prompts.json (about 93k chars) and the fix-node-pty-perms script were also not reviewed.

comments.body: serve_command() builds a `python -m pagedserve.cli serve ...` command with many flags: --served-model-name, --attn-backend, --block-size, --enable-cuda-graphs, --enable-prefix-caching, --quantization, --tensor-parallel-size, --max-num-seqs and others. pagedserve/cli.py is not in this diff, so I cannot confirm that these flags exist or that the module runs via `-m`. The unit test only checks the generated strings, so a wrong flag would be caught only when the worker starts on a GPU. Separately, if the CLI turns CUDA graphs on by default for cuda, CUDA_GRAPHS=0 would have no effect. A human should check the command against the real CLI, ideally by running `pagedserve serve --help` or a smoke start.

On the non-stream path, `httpx.Response(200, content=raw).json()` raises JSONDecodeError (a ValueError) if the server returns a non-JSON body, for example from a route like /health. That is not an httpx.HTTPError, so it escapes the handler instead of returning an error dict. Catch ValueError and yield a worker error.

comments.body: This enables CUDA-graph capture for paged_triton on the claim that its decode step reads only static device tensors. The backend's forward/decode code is not in this diff, so I can't verify that claim. Capture is unsafe if the backend does any of the following during decode: host syncs (.item() or .tolist()), per-call host-derived grid sizes or num_splits (the split-K choice may depend on live batch or context), or allocations outside the graph pool. The new tests that would catch this are GPU-only and cannot be seen to have run. A human should confirm the backend's decode path is capture-safe, or confirm that the GPU tests pass on a real device.

This change reduces the tile from 32 to 16 for 7→8 groups at D=64. That is plausibly a register-pressure fix, but the numerical and performance effect cannot be verified here. The docstring also says the tile always divides block_size. min(block_size, tile) does not guarantee that for a block_size that is a multiple of 16 but not a power of two (for example 48 with tile 32). That case may be rejected elsewhere or may be a pre-existing limitation, but it is worth confirming.
